Plot movement tracks

Source: R/draw.track.R
draw.track.Rd

Draws the trajectory of each individual, with locations optionally coloured by any column of the data, such as the movement phase from class.mov, the behavioural state from fitHMM.wrap or the cluster_id from get.arp.

Usage

draw.track(
  data,
  colour.col = NULL,
  ids = NULL,
  id.col = "ID",
  time.col = "time",
  coord.names = c("x", "y"),
  colour.path = FALSE,
  km = FALSE,
  palette = NULL,
  point.size = 0.6
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or an object of class disperseR.

colour.col

Character. Optional name of the column used to colour the locations. Default is NULL (no colour).

ids

Character vector. Optional selection of individuals to plot. Default is NULL (all individuals).

id.col

Character. Name of the column containing individual identifiers. Default is "ID".

time.col

Character. Name of the column containing timestamps, used to order the locations. Default is "time".

coord.names

Character vector of length 2 with the names of the X and Y coordinate columns. Default is c("x", "y").

colour.path

Logical. If TRUE, the path between locations is also coloured by colour.col; otherwise it is drawn in grey. Default is FALSE.

km

Logical. If TRUE, projected coordinates in metres are shown in kilometres. Default is FALSE.

palette

Optional named character vector of colours for the values of colour.col. If NULL, a default palette is used for the phase column and the default ggplot2 palette otherwise.

point.size

Numeric. Size of the location points. Default is 0.6.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

With one individual the plot keeps the true aspect ratio (coord_equal). With several individuals each one is drawn in its own panel with free scales.

Examples

draw.track(sim_tracks, time.col = "timestamp", km = TRUE)


eps <- get.epsilon(sim_states)
#> Computing a global threshold using all data combined.
arp <- get.arp(sim_states, epsilon = eps, delta.days = 2, pct.state1 = 0.2)
mov <- class.mov(link.arp(arp, thres = 24 * 3600))
draw.track(mov, colour.col = "phase", km = TRUE)

draw.track(mov, colour.col = "phase", ids = "M01", colour.path = TRUE, km = TRUE)
